identity.title: Position: Certified Robustness Does Not (Yet) Imply Model Security

problem.claim: The paper addresses how certified robustness against adversarial examples can become meaningfully deployable in real-world AI applications.

gap.claim: It identifies unresolved gaps: detection may not distinguish relevant cases, practitioners lack clear criteria for evaluating certification schemes, and users’ expectations of guaranteed robustness may create security risks.

contributions.claim: It identifies three critical deployment and security gaps in current certified-robustness research.
It proposes concrete steps for the certification research community to address these challenges and move toward practical applicability.

narrative_sequence.summary: Certified robustness is promoted against adversarial examples, but substantial challenges remain for real-world deployment.
The paper highlights detection without distinction, missing evaluation criteria, and security risks linked to expectations of guaranteed robustness.
It calls for concrete research steps aimed at addressing these challenges and improving practical applicability.

source_observation.claim: The abstract pairs a broad deployment goal with distinct technical, evaluation, and expectation-related obstacles.

lessons.interpretation: Separating obstacle types can make a position paper’s diagnosis more actionable than treating deployment difficulty as one undifferentiated problem.
lessons.application: Frame a research agenda by mapping each deployment goal to separately named failure modes, practitioner decision criteria, and user-facing security risks.
lessons.exception: This framing is less suitable when the work studies a narrowly defined mechanism with a single well-specified failure mode.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the concrete steps proposed in detail.
No empirical results, formal proofs, certification schemes, or comparisons are reported.
The scope and operational meaning of “detection without distinction” are not defined in the abstract.
